why:
What leaves the window for a pane's daemon, in what order, when somebody types, pastes or an input method commits. The daemon encodes every keystroke against the pane's own terminal modes and is the only writer to the pane, so what the core decides is only what the keymap takes first and what a keystroke is by the time it leaves: option-as-alt applied, and the setting sent beside it so the daemon's encoder applies the same one.

A case is a list of steps and the expectation is the ordered trace of every event sent, since order is the property a single route keeps and the one worth pinning. `given.optionAsAlt` sets the config's option-as-alt; absent is never.

cases.name: a keystroke the keymap does not take leaves as the keystroke itself
cases.why: The daemon encodes it against the pane's modes, which only it can see, so nothing is encoded here.

cases.name: an arrow is a keystroke like any other
cases.why: Application cursor mode decides between SS3 and CSI, and the daemon can see which is on. The keymap no longer takes arrows for a second route, so none of them races the keys around it.

cases.name: a bound chord becomes its own bytes and never reaches the encoder
cases.why: cmd+backspace is readline's unix-line-discard, ctrl+U, whatever the pane has negotiated. The bytes go as they are.

cases.name: option as alt is applied before the keystroke leaves, and named beside it
cases.why: macOS reports option as spent when it composed a character, so the daemon's encoder could not tell alt+b from a typed ∫. The core takes the spend back and replaces the text with what the layout would have produced without option, and names the setting so the encoder agrees.

cases.name: a paste leaves as a paste
cases.why: The daemon fences it when the program asked for bracketed paste and holds one that would run several lines as typed, both of which need the pane's modes. Not confirmed until somebody says so.

cases.name: a paste somebody confirmed says so
cases.why: The answer to a held paste is the same paste, marked, so the daemon writes it rather than holding it again.

cases.name: an empty paste sends nothing
cases.why: A paste of nothing has nothing to fence or hold, and an event for it would be a message for the daemon to throw away.

cases.name: what an input method commits is written as it stands
cases.why: A commit is text, neither a keystroke for the encoder to reinterpret under the kitty protocol nor a paste to fence, which is how Ghostty's own surface writes one.
